I have enjoyed the natural sciences since my earliest boyhood, and even just returned from a museum of natural history. The natural sciences are one of the defining features of the Occident since the Renaissance; no other culture has developed a scientific view of nature. Science is a method to study the natural world and its actions, and has enjoyed immense success. It makes no moral statements, however, nor was it ever intended to; its conclusions are moreover tentative, which is something often forgotten.

I do not associate the sciences with atheism in itself; I long ago outgrew the juvenile stage wherein I thought the natural sciences could at all demonstrate anything against God. There are many atheist scientists, yes, but just as many of the luminaries of science were and are Christian. Indeed, the natural sciences have furnished several proofs of His existence.

As concerns global warming or climate change, I freely confess my ambivalence. I remember books only a dozen years ago wherein water or air pollution was viewed the dominant threat, and when many or most scientists found a connexion between fossil fuels and increased temperatures probable, and spoke in conditional statements and with due hesitation. There was not to nearly the same degree the certainty or alarmism one finds more recently.
